findings.title: Denial cache defeats the newly-created-resource fix
findings.body: When a check is denied, the result is cached for 30s under (user, action, name, parent). If a user checks a resource before its permission is written, as happens in the create flow, every later check for that resource returns deny from this cache without querying the DB. The resource only becomes accessible once the entry expires, which is the stale-access problem this PR is meant to fix. Nothing ever invalidates the cache when permissions change.

findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous and keyed on raw subject UID
findings.body: The key is built by joining fields with '_', and names, folder UIDs and actions can themselves contain '_'. Two different requests can therefore produce the same key and wrongly share a cached denial. The key also uses the raw request subject, which may be a numeric ID or a UID, so it is inconsistent with the normalized UID used for permCache keys. In addition, the key omits identity type, so for anonymous subjects it uses the subject ID rather than the anonymous namespace key.

findings.title: Cache usage metric double-counted / misreported
findings.body: A cached-permission miss records cache usage 'false' at line 137. On a denial-cache hit, line 118 records 'true' but nothing records the permission-cache lookup. As a result, the cache hit-rate metric is skewed.

findings.title: Deny-cache test doesn't prove precedence
findings.body: The test seeds permCache with dashboards:uid:dash1 set to false, so the cached-permission path would deny anyway. The fallback path would also deny because the fake store has no permissions. The test therefore passes even without the denial cache and does not verify the behavior its comment claims.
